name: Otmar Szafnauer
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; joined Ford Motor Company at 22 and obtained a racing license at 25, but his F1 career began at 34 with BAR in 1998.
early_history_summary: Born in a small Romanian village without running water, Szafnauer moved to Detroit at age 7. He earned an electrical engineering degree from Wayne State and an MBA from University of Detroit Mercy, then joined Ford in 1986. He began racing Formula Ford as a hobby in his mid-20s but did not enter Formula 1 until 1998.
family_context_summary: Born to an American father of German descent and a Romanian mother in a village without running water; family emigrated to Detroit when he was 7.
evidence_summary: Szafnauer's path to F1 was unusually long; he worked at Ford from age 22 and only entered F1 at 34. No material, independently verifiable milestone by age 26 was found.

name: Yannick Noah
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1983 French Open singles title at age 23, becoming the first Frenchman to win the tournament in 37 years, and reached world No. 3 in singles and No. 1 in doubles by age 26 in 1986.
early_history_summary: Born in France to a Cameroonian footballer father and French mother, Noah grew up in Cameroon where he was discovered at age 11 by Arthur Ashe during a tennis clinic. Ashe recommended him to the French Tennis Federation, which brought him to its training center in Nice in 1971. He turned professional in 1977 at age 17 and won his first top-level singles title in 1978 in Manila.
family_context_summary: Born in Sedan, France to a Cameroonian professional footballer father (Zacharie Noah) and a French mother; family moved to Cameroon after the father's sports injury when Yannick was 3.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Arthur Ashe discovery, FFT training center, early specialization, sports family
evidence_summary: Noah was discovered at 11 by Arthur Ashe in Cameroon and channeled into the French Tennis Federation's elite training center in Nice, providing a structured pipeline from a young age. His father's background as a professional footballer gave him a sports-oriented family culture. The FFT pipeline, combined with Ashe's personal advocacy, concentrated opportunity and coaching resources around him from age 11, enabling him to turn pro at 17 and win the French Open at 23.
starting_point: Born in Sedan, France to a Cameroonian professional footballer father and French mother; family relocated to Cameroon when he was 3 after his father's sports injury.
current_position: Former tennis player turned popular music performer; inducted into International Tennis Hall of Fame in 2005; resides in France.

trajectory.event: Discovered by Arthur Ashe at a tennis clinic in Yaoundé, Cameroon, and brought to the French Tennis Federation training center in Nice.
Turned professional and won his first pro title on the Italian Spring Satellite circuit.
Won his first top-level singles title in Manila, Philippines, defeating Peter Feigl in the final.
Won the French Open singles title, becoming the first Frenchman to win the tournament in 37 years and the first black man to claim the title.
Reached career-high singles ranking of world No. 3 in July and attained the world No. 1 doubles ranking in August.
Retired from professional tennis after a nearly two-decade career with 23 singles titles and 16 doubles titles.
Inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

name: Desireless
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; she was working as a fashion designer in her early 20s and did not begin her music career until meeting producer Jean-Michel Rivat in 1984 at age 31, with her hit 'Voyage Voyage' released in 1986 at age 33.
early_history_summary: Born Claudie Fritsch-Mentrop in Paris, she grew up in Tréport and became a fashion designer in the early 1970s. She traveled to India in 1980 and began singing with jazz, new wave, and R&B bands in the early 1980s before meeting producer Jean-Michel Rivat in 1984, which led to her breakthrough single 'Voyage Voyage' in 1986.
family_context_summary: Born in Paris, France; grew up in Tréport. Not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Desireless had no material music milestone by age 26; she was a fashion designer in her early 20s and only entered music in the early 1980s. Her breakthrough came at 33 with 'Voyage Voyage' in 1986.

name: Yacouba Sawadogo
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he was working as a salesman at a local market after attending Koranic school in Mali. His pioneering zaï soil restoration work began around 1980 when he was approximately 34.
early_history_summary: Born in Gourga, Burkina Faso, Sawadogo attended Koranic school in Mali before returning to Yatenga to work as a salesman. Severe droughts in the Sahel region from 1972 to 1984 prompted him to begin experimenting with traditional zaï planting pit techniques around 1980, eventually creating a 40-hectare forest on barren land and earning the nickname 'the man who stopped the desert.'
family_context_summary: Born in Gourga, Yatenga Province, Burkina Faso; had no formal education and never learned to read or write.
evidence_summary: Sawadogo had no material milestone by age 26; he was a market salesman with no formal education. His internationally recognized work on zaï soil restoration began around 1980 when he was approximately 34, and his major awards came decades later.

name: Roddy Piper
milestone_by_age_26: Won the NWA Americas Heavyweight Championship in March 1976 at age 21, and by age 26 was a five-time NWA Americas champion and seven-time tag team champion in the Los Angeles territory.
early_history_summary: Born in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Piper left home as a young teenager after conflicts with his father and lived in youth hostels. He was an amateur boxer and won the 165-pound Amateur Wrestling Championship of Manitoba at 15. His first professional wrestling match was at age 15 in 1969 in Churchill, Manitoba. By the mid-1970s he was a top villain in NWA Hollywood Wrestling, winning the Americas Heavyweight title five times.
family_context_summary: Born to an RCMP/CN police officer father and Scottish-Canadian mother; left home as a young teenager and lived in youth hostels, sleeping on gymnasium floors.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a police officer with no known wrestling connection.
primary_early_advantage_tags: left home young, street immersion, amateur wrestling, early pro debut, adversity
evidence_summary: Piper's early career was defined by adversity and self-creation; he left home as a young teenager, lived in youth hostels, and immersed himself directly in the wrestling world from age 15. His amateur boxing and wrestling background gave him foundational physical skills, and he learned professional wrestling on the job in Canadian and American territories. By 21 he was a champion in the NWA Hollywood territory, building the character work and mic skills that would make him a wrestling icon.
starting_point: Born in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan to a CN police officer father and Scottish-Canadian mother; left home as a young teenager after conflicts with his father and lived in youth hostels.
current_position: Died July 31, 2015 at age 61 in Hollywood, California; final role as professional wrestler and actor, best known for WWF career and starring in 'They Live.'

trajectory.event: First professional wrestling match in Churchill, Manitoba, beginning his career as a jobber in Canadian territories.
Won the 165-pound Amateur Wrestling Championship of Manitoba.
Won the NWA Americas Heavyweight Championship in Los Angeles, becoming a top villain in NWA Hollywood Wrestling.
Held the NWA Americas Heavyweight title five times and the tag team championship seven times in the Los Angeles territory.
Joined the WWF (now WWE) and quickly became one of the most hated villains in wrestling history.
Headlined the first WrestleMania at Madison Square Garden, a landmark event in professional wrestling history.
Starred as Nada in John Carpenter's cult film 'They Live,' establishing a parallel acting career.
Died of a heart attack on July 31 in Hollywood, California.

name: Svetlana Zakharova
milestone_by_age_26: Promoted to principal dancer at the Mariinsky Ballet in 1997 at age 18, after joining the company at 17 and being the youngest contestant to win second prize at the Vaganova-Prix competition in 1995.
early_history_summary: Born in Lutsk, Ukrainian SSR, Zakharova began folk dancing at age 6 and was accepted into the Kyiv Choreography School at 10. After six years there, she entered the Vaganova-Prix competition in 1995 as the youngest contestant, won second prize, and was invited to the Vaganova Academy's graduating class, skipping two grades in an unprecedented move. She joined the Mariinsky Ballet in 1996 and was promoted to principal dancer at 18 in 1997.
family_context_summary: Born in Lutsk, Ukrainian SSR; mother enrolled her in folk dancing at age 6. No documented family dance background or financial privilege.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; mother took initiative to enroll her in dance but no known professional dance background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kyiv Choreography School, Vaganova Academy, Mariinsky Ballet, early specialization, phenomenal physique, sustained coaching
evidence_summary: Zakharova's trajectory was defined by elite institutional pipelines: Kyiv Choreography School from age 10, then the Vaganova Academy where she skipped two grades (unprecedented). Her phenomenal physique was noted immediately at the Vaganova-Prix competition. Sustained coaching from Valeria Sulegina, Elena Evteeva, and Olga Moiseyeva accelerated her rise. The Soviet/Russian ballet ecosystem provided the world's most concentrated ballet infrastructure, enabling her promotion to principal at 18.
starting_point: Born in Lutsk, Ukrainian SSR, Soviet Union; mother enrolled her in folk dancing at age 6, and she was sent away to the Kyiv Choreography School at age 10.
current_position: Prima ballerina of the Bolshoi Ballet and étoile of La Scala; acting rector of the Moscow State Academy of Choreography; resides in Russia.

trajectory.event: Accepted into the Kyiv Choreography School after auditioning, beginning formal ballet training away from her family.
Won second prize at the Vaganova-Prix competition as the youngest contestant and was invited to the Vaganova Academy graduating class, skipping two grades for the first time in the school's history.
Joined the Mariinsky Ballet and debuted as Maria in The Fountain of Bakhchisarai.
Promoted to principal dancer at the Mariinsky Ballet, with Olga Moiseyeva as her permanent coach and mentor.
Joined the Bolshoi Ballet as prima ballerina after receiving an invitation from Vladimir Vasiliev.
Became étoile of La Scala in Milan, expanding her international profile.

name: Durdy Bayramov
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; he was still a student at the Surikov Art Institute in Moscow (attended 1959-1965) and did not join the USSR Union of Artists until 1965 at age 27. His celebrated painting 'Peaceful Land' came in 1969.
early_history_summary: Born in Baýramaly, Turkmen SSR, Bayramov lost both parents at a young age and lived as a homeless child before being placed in an orphanage. He was mentored by artist Gennadiy Brusentsov, who recognized his talent, and attended the Shota Rustaveli Turkmen State College of Arts before entering the prestigious Surikov Art Institute in Moscow in 1959, studying under Dmitry Mochalsky until 1965.
family_context_summary: Orphaned at a young age; lived as a homeless child before being placed in an orphanage in Serdar (Kyzyl-Arvat), enduring starvation and post-war devastation during World War II.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents died when he was young.
evidence_summary: Bayramov was still a student at the Surikov Art Institute during his age-26 year (1964), completing his degree in 1965. While he had strong mentorship from Brusentsov and Mochalsky, no independently verifiable material milestone occurred by age 26. His professional career began after graduation at 27.

name: Andreja Pejić
milestone_by_age_26: Walked both men's and women's Paris fashion shows for Jean-Paul Gaultier and men's shows for Marc Jacobs in January 2011 at age 19, becoming an internationally recognized androgynous model; appeared on the controversial Dossier Journal cover in May 2011.
early_history_summary: Born in Tuzla, Yugoslavia (now Bosnia and Herzegovina), Pejić fled to Serbia as a refugee during the Bosnian War and later moved to Melbourne, Australia in 2000 as a political refugee. She was scouted just before her 17th birthday in 2008 while working at McDonald's. By 19, she was walking major Paris fashion shows for Jean-Paul Gaultier and Marc Jacobs, gaining international attention for her androgynous look.
family_context_summary: Born to a Bosnian Croat father and Serb mother who divorced shortly after her birth; family fled as refugees during the Bosnian War, settling in a refugee camp near Belgrade before emigrating to Melbourne, Australia in 2000.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no known family connections to fashion or modeling.
primary_early_advantage_tags: androgynous beauty, refugee background, gender fluidity wave, Gaultier discovery, unique look
evidence_summary: Pejić's breakthrough was driven by an extraordinary physical edge — her androgynous appearance at 6'1' was so striking that it changed how the fashion industry categorized models, enabling her to walk both men's and women's shows at Paris Fashion Week at 19. The rising cultural wave around gender fluidity in the early 2010s amplified her uniqueness. Her refugee background and transgender identity created significant adversity but also a distinctive perspective that the fashion industry found compelling.
starting_point: Born in Tuzla, Yugoslavia to a Bosnian Croat father and Serb mother who divorced shortly after her birth; family fled as refugees during the Bosnian War and emigrated to Melbourne, Australia in 2000.
current_position: Former model and actress; one of the world's most recognizable transgender models since coming out in 2014; resides in the United States.

trajectory.event: Family moved to Melbourne, Australia as political refugees after the NATO bombing of Yugoslavia.
Scouted as a model just before her 17th birthday while working at McDonald's in Melbourne.
Walked both men's and women's Paris fashion shows for Jean-Paul Gaultier and men's shows for Marc Jacobs, gaining international recognition.
Appeared on the cover of Dossier Journal, which was censored by US bookstores for being deemed too risqué.
Publicly came out as a transgender woman, becoming one of the first internationally successful models to transition publicly.
Walked her first runway as a fully transitioned woman at Giles Deacon's fall show during London Fashion Week.

name: Christopher Alexander
milestone_by_age_26: Completed the first-ever PhD in Architecture at Harvard University in 1962 at age 25-26, with his dissertation 'The Synthesis of Form' later published as a seminal book in 1964.
early_history_summary: Born in Vienna, Alexander emigrated to England with his family following the Anschluss. He attended the Dragon School and Oundle School before winning the top open scholarship to Trinity College, Cambridge in 1954, where he earned a BA in Architecture and an MA in Mathematics. He moved to the US in 1958 to pursue his doctorate at Harvard, while also working at MIT in transportation theory and computer science. He completed his PhD in 1962, the first in Architecture ever awarded at Harvard.
family_context_summary: Born in Vienna, Austria to a Catholic father and Jewish mother; family emigrated to England following the Anschluss, providing access to elite British schooling.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no known family architecture background, but family was sufficiently established to support emigration and elite education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Trinity College Cambridge, Harvard PhD, MIT, elite schooling, cross-disciplinary depth, emigration
evidence_summary: Alexander's early trajectory was defined by elite institutional pipelines: Dragon School, Oundle School, Trinity College Cambridge (top open scholarship at 18), then Harvard and MIT. His cross-disciplinary depth spanning architecture, mathematics, transportation theory, and cognitive studies was exceptional and scarce. The first-ever PhD in Architecture at Harvard by age 26 was a material, verifiable milestone. His Jewish heritage and forced emigration from Austria provided a constraint that channeled him into the British educational elite.
starting_point: Born in Vienna, Austria to a Catholic father and Jewish mother; family emigrated to England following the Anschluss, providing access to elite British education.
current_position: Died March 17, 2022 at age 85 in Binsted, Sussex, England; final role as emeritus professor of architecture at UC Berkeley and founder of the Center for Environmental Structure.

trajectory.event: Awarded the top open scholarship to Trinity College, Cambridge, initially in chemistry and physics, later switching to mathematics and architecture.
Moved to the United States to pursue doctoral studies at Harvard and research at MIT in transportation theory and computer science.
Completed the first-ever PhD in Architecture at Harvard University with his dissertation 'The Synthesis of Form.'
Appointed professor of architecture at UC Berkeley, where he would teach for nearly 40 years.
Founded the Center for Environmental Structure in Berkeley.
Published 'A Pattern Language,' his most influential work, which became a perennial bestseller and influenced fields from architecture to software design.
Died on March 17 in Binsted, Sussex, England.

name: Mario Terán
milestone_by_age_26: Executed Che Guevara by firing squad on October 9, 1967 at age 25 in La Higuera, Bolivia, an event of major historical significance.
early_history_summary: Born in Cochabamba, Bolivia to a merchant father and mother, Terán joined the Bolivian military in 1959 at age 17. He served as a sergeant in Company A of Bolivia's Manchego Regiment. In October 1967, he was the soldier who executed the captured revolutionary Che Guevara, drawing the short straw among his unit. He lived the rest of his life in relative anonymity.
family_context_summary: Born in Cochabamba, Bolivia to a merchant father (46 years old at Mario's birth) and mother (45 years old); little is known about his early life beyond this.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; father was a merchant with no known military connections.
evidence_summary: Terán's milestone was a single historical event rather than a career built on early advantages. He was an ordinary Bolivian Army sergeant with no documented family advantages, mentorship, or elite training. His unit was trained by US Green Beret and CIA operatives, but this was institutional rather than personal advantage. The execution of Che Guevara was a product of Cold War geopolitical circumstances rather than individual merit or preparation.
starting_point: Born in Cochabamba, Bolivia to a merchant father and mother; little is known about his early life beyond his parents' ages and occupations.
current_position: Died March 10, 2022 at age 79 in La Paz, Bolivia; lived in anonymity and financial penury after retiring from the military.

trajectory.event: Joined the Bolivian military, serving as a sergeant in Company A of the Manchego Regiment.
Executed Che Guevara by firing squad in a schoolhouse in La Higuera, Bolivia, after drawing the short straw among his unit.
Received free cataract surgery from Cuban doctors under Operación Milagro, a program launched after Evo Morales was elected president of Bolivia.
Died on March 10 in La Paz, Bolivia, after a long illness.

name: Ana Mendieta
milestone_by_age_26: Created the landmark performance work 'Rape Scene' in 1973 at age 24 and began the influential Silueta series of earth-body artworks in 1973-1974, establishing her signature artistic practice by age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Havana, Cuba to a wealthy, politically prominent family, Mendieta was sent to the United States at age 12 via Operation Pedro Pan in 1961, separated from her parents and placed in foster homes and institutions in Iowa. She earned a BA in art (1969-1972) and MA in painting (1972) at the University of Iowa, then enrolled in the MFA Intermedia program under Hans Breder, where she created her first performance works in 1972 and the seminal 'Rape Scene' in 1973.
family_context_summary: Born to a wealthy Cuban family prominent in politics and society; father was an attorney and nephew of former president Carlos Mendieta, mother was a chemist and researcher. Family wealth and status were disrupted by exile.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an attorney involved in Cuban politics; mother was a chemist and researcher from a sugar mill owning family. Educated, upper-class background but disrupted by exile and father's 18-year imprisonment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: exile, Operation Pedro Pan, family separation, feminist art movement, Hans Breder mentorship, earth-body art
evidence_summary: Mendieta's artistic practice was fundamentally shaped by the trauma of exile from Cuba at age 12, separation from her family, and movement through foster homes in Iowa. This adversity became the raw material for her earth-body artworks exploring displacement, identity, and belonging. The University of Iowa's Intermedia program under Hans Breder provided the academic framework for her interdisciplinary approach. The emerging feminist art movement of the early 1970s provided a structural wave that amplified her work. Her family's upper-class Cuban background provided cultural capital but was largely inaccessible after exile.
starting_point: Born in Havana, Cuba to a wealthy, politically prominent family; father was an attorney and nephew of a former Cuban president, mother was a chemist and researcher.
current_position: Died September 8, 1985 at age 36 in New York City after falling from her 34th-floor apartment; final role as performance and earth-body artist.

trajectory.event: Sent to the United States via Operation Pedro Pan, separated from her parents and placed in refugee camps and foster homes in Iowa.
Created her first performance works as a graduate student in the Intermedia program at the University of Iowa under Hans Breder.
Staged the landmark performance 'Rape Scene' in response to the rape and murder of a fellow student, and began the Silueta series of earth-body artworks.
Completed her MFA in Intermedia at the University of Iowa and moved to New York City.
Died on September 8 after falling from her 34th-floor apartment in New York City, with the circumstances remaining controversial.

name: Alfredo Ferrari
milestone_by_age_26: Credited with the design of the Ferrari 750 Monza racing car body by 1954 at age 22, and proposed the 1.5L DOHC V6 engine for Formula Two alongside Vittorio Jano at the end of 1955 at age 23, before his death at 24 from Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
early_history_summary: Born in Modena, Italy to Enzo Ferrari and Laura Dominica Garello, Alfredo was groomed from childhood to succeed his father. He studied economics in Bologna before switching to mechanical engineering in Switzerland, and earned an engineering diploma from a technical institute in Modena. He worked directly at Ferrari from the early 1950s, contributing to the 750 Monza design and proposing the V6 engine that would become the Dino series. He died at 24 from muscular dystrophy.
family_context_summary: Born to Enzo Ferrari, the legendary automaker and founder of Scuderia Ferrari, and Laura Dominica Garello in Modena, Italy. Enzo retired from racing upon Alfredo's birth and groomed him as his successor.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was Enzo Ferrari, one of the most influential figures in automotive and racing history; Alfredo was immersed in the Ferrari racing operation from childhood, with direct access to the factory, engineers, and racing culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Enzo Ferrari son, Ferrari factory access, Modena racing ecosystem, Vittorio Jano mentorship, automotive engineering, degenerative illness
evidence_summary: Alfredo Ferrari's entire career was defined by inherited access: as Enzo Ferrari's only son, he had direct access to the Ferrari factory, racing operations, and world-class engineers like Vittorio Jano and Aurelio Lampredi from childhood. The Modena ecosystem was the global center of Italian racing. His engineering contributions to the 750 Monza and the Dino V6 concept were real but deeply enabled by his family position. His degenerative illness (Duchenne muscular dystrophy) created urgency and limited his output, making his achievements remarkable but truncated.
starting_point: Born in Modena, Italy to Enzo Ferrari, the legendary automaker and racing team manager, and Laura Dominica Garello; groomed from birth as his father's successor in the Ferrari enterprise.
current_position: Died June 30, 1956 at age 24 in Modena, Italy from Duchenne muscular dystrophy; final role as automotive engineer at Ferrari contributing to the 750 Monza and Dino V6 engine.

trajectory.event: Credited with the body design concept for the Ferrari 750 Monza racing car, which debuted at Monza and took first and second positions.
Proposed the development of a 1.5L DOHC V6 engine for Formula Two racing alongside engineer Vittorio Jano.
Died on June 30 in Modena from Duchenne muscular dystrophy, which had progressively limited his physical capabilities.
Posthumously honored when Enzo Ferrari named the Dino series of racing and road cars after him, using the V6 engine he had proposed.
